title_content.content: Enantioselective and Regiodivergent Skeletal Transformations of 1,2,3-Thiadiazoles to Alkylidene Dihydrothiophenes

paragraph_content.content: Cunzhi Chen, Youwei Chen, Hongguang Du, Jiaxi Xu, and Zhanhui Yang*

image_caption.content: ABSTRACT: By leveraging the Rh-catalyzed asymmetric skeletal editing of 1,2,3-thiadiazoles, we successfully achieve the ligandcontrolled enantioselective and regiodivergent synthesis of structurally diverse 2- and 3-alkylidene 2,3-dihydrothiophenes. Late-stage structural editing of complex natural and drug molecules is also enabled.

However, very little attention has been paid to alkylidene dihydrothiophenes (type I, type II, and type III), which possess 3-dimensional-structures and one stereocenter (Scheme 1A). These structural properties cater to the well-recognized concept�escape from flatland, making them promising scafolds in drug development campaigns. The enantioselective synthesis of these molecules nonetheless is highly challenging. The limited synthetic routes mainly relied on the dearomative functionaliztion of parent thiophene rings (Scheme 1B).<sup>4−6</sup> In 2021, Sun and Houk reported the chiral phosphoric acid (CPA)-catalyzed enantioselective dearomative functionalization of thiophenes by means of 1,10-conjugate addition, giving type I structures.<sup>5</sup> In 2022, Buchwald and Liu disclosed the enantioselective synthesis of type II products via CuH-catalyzed dearomative addition of 3- vinylthiophenes to ketones.<sup>6</sup> Despite these state-of-the-art advances, new synthetic methods based on diferent synthetic logics are still in demand.

Herein, by adoption of a ligand-controlled tactic (Scheme 1D), the above challenges are well addressed. Our work provides a novel synthetic access to enantiopure 3- dimensional alkylidene-2,3-dihydrothiophenes, which might be used as a potential pharmacore in future drug development campaigns.

We first optimized the chiral ligands and other reaction parameters, revealing two sets of optimal conditions (see Tables S1 and S2 in Supporting Information): with (4R, 5R)-DIOP enantiopure 2-alkylidene-2,3-dihydrothiophenes are exclusively furnished (Conditions A), while with (R)-Cy-BINAP the regioreversed 3-alkylidene-2,3-dihydrothiophenes were enantioselectively synthesized (Conditions B). We first evaluated the synthesis of enantiopure type III products 3 (Figure 1A). The reactions showed a broad substrate scope and functional group tolerance. The skeletal editing of 5- aryl-substituted 1,2,3-thiadiazole-4-carboxylates (1a−1o) proceeded smoothly, regardless of the functionalities on the aryl rings, furnishing 3aA−3oA in 57−95% yields and 96−99% ee. The other regioisomers were formed in such a small amount that they could not be isolated. Well tolerated functional groups include halogens (3fA−3iA, 3jA), cyano (3lA), nitro (3kA), and fur-2-yl (3mA), and thiophen-2-yl (3nA). Aromatization occurred for 3eA, accounting for the low yield (32%). However, shortening the reaction time to 80 min significantly improved the yield to 92% (96% ee). In addition, 5-methyl, 5-chloro, and 5-bromo thiadiazoles were also demonstrated as viable substrates, converting to desired products in 90−94% ee (3pA−3rA). The absolute configuration of 3rA was unambiguously assigned by single-crystal X-ray difraction (CCDC: 2404905). The ester group on the 4-position can also be diversified. For example, the reaction of 3-bromopropyl 1,2,3- thiadiazole-4-carboxylate delivered 3sA in 93% yield and 86% ee, with the labile C(sp<sup>3</sup>)−Br bond remaining untouched. Replacement of the ester group with secondary amide slightly lowered the yields, whereas improved the enantioselectivity to 99% ee, as demonstrated by the enantioselective formation of 3tA−3zA.

A number of allenes were also assessed under Conditions A. Diversifying the ester group ((±)-2H−2O) or replacing the methyl of (±)-2A with substituted phenyls ((±)-2B−2F) and propyl ((±)-2G) did not afect the regio- or enantioselectivities. Desired products were obtained in 44−99% yields and 90−97% ee. In addition, a sulfonyl allene was also amenable, giving 3bO in 90% yield with 90% ee.

By changing (4R,5R)-DIOP to (R)-Cy-BINAP (Conditions B), we accomplished the regio-reversed synthesis of type II products (Figure 1B). Desired products 4aA−4dA, 4gA, 4hA, and 4jA−4lA were produced in 50−76% yields and 92−99% ee, with regioselective ratios varying from 3:1 to 17:1. Apparently, the regioselectivity is quite sensitive to the electronic properties of the aromatic substituents. The reactions of four additional allenes (4bH, 4aB, 4aD, 4aE) gave excellent enantiocontrol (>99% ee) and almost unchanged regioselectivity (4.5:1 or 4:1 rr). The other regioisomers can be separated by column chromatography. For instance, 3aA was isolated in 8% yield (96% ee). Notably, the substrate scope under Conditions B is a bit limited (see Scheme S2 in the Supporting Information). For example, 5-methyl or 5-bromo-1,2,3-thiadiazoles failed to undergo the skeletal editing and remained intact.

The scalability was demonstrated by the 1 mmol scale reaction, in which 3aA was obtained in 89% yield and 96% ee (Scheme 2A). Oxidation of 3aA with excess m-CPBA or reduction with NaBH −CoCl led to sulfone 5 or transdihydrothiphene 6 in good yields without erosion of the enantiopurity (Scheme 2B). It deserves mention that the exocyclic C�C bond is more susceptible to reduction than the endocyclic one. Deuterium-labeled allene 2E-d aforded deuterium-incorporated product 3aE-d in 90% yield and 95% ee (Scheme 2C). The deuterium of the starting material was almost all retained in the product.

Our protocol can be applied to the late-stage diversification of natural and pharmaceutically relevant molecules (Scheme 2D). Five 1,2,3-thiadiazoles derived from D-galactopyranose (7a), cholesterol (7b), stigmasterol (7c), diosgenin (7d), and pregnenolone (7e) were transformed eficiently, giving 8aA− 8eA in 56−85% yields and 95.5:4.5−98:2 dr. These highly diastereo- and enantiopure structures may arguably serve as potential lead compounds in drug discovery. Dehydroabietylamine and oleylamine were also late-stage modified, giving 8fA in 57% yield, 99:1 dr and 8gA in 60% yield, 99% ee, respectively. On the other hand, the regio-reversed skeletal transformation can also be applied in the structural modification of natural products, as exemplified by the synthesis of9aA and 9bA from Dgalactopyranose and cholesterol. These reactions in the presence of complex structures further expand the functionality tolerance.

In conclusion, we have developed a strategically novel rhodium-catalyzed and ligand-controlled regiodivergent and enantioselective synthetic route to alkylidene-2,3-dihydrothiophenes through diatomic skeletal editing of 1,2,3-thiadiazoles with allenoates. Both types of products are synthesized in up to 99% yield and up to 99% ee. Late-stage structural modifications of complex natural and drug molecules are performed, rendering chiral and 3-dimensional chemical spaces with higher levels of molecular complexity. It is anticipated that our synthetic routes to these underexplored enantiopure 3-dimensional alkylidene-2,3-dihydrothiophenes will ofer compelling opportunities and provide novel lead compounds for future drug discoveries and developments.
